emails.tone: Matter-of-fact and unhurried. Confident because it is specific, not because it is loud: short declarative sentences, a claim followed by the literal thing it means, clauses appended after an em dash. The register of someone describing a tool to a peer who will check it.
emails.call_to_action: Start for free — sign up, no credit card, and point an agent at your own handbook docs: https://app.orqagent.com/sign-up
emails.subject_strategy: This reader already knows a Slack answer-bot over company docs is possible; the subject's job is to say that it is now something available rather than something to build, in their nouns — Slack, handbook, docs — with no hype word and no question mark. It must not promise better search or faster answers, and it must not read like a generic AI product launch, which is the mail they have already deleted this month.

brief.voice_notes: Write in English (the request and the audience research are English) even though the company publishes bilingually; if a product label is French in the console, give it plainly in English. Use the company's own nouns — agent, system prompt, knowledge base file, run, Playground — and this buyer's nouns: handbook, policy question, channel, docs. 'We' for the company, 'you' for the reader, no individual signature (none is captured in the brand voice). Professional and polished as requested means plain and precise, not formal-corporate: no exclamation marks, no rhetorical questions stacked at the top, no 'imagine if'.
